correctness.rationale: The object-specific modulus lower bound is sound. At every level k, each base-7 y-word using only digits {0,1,2,5,6} gives a fully retained horizontal row; these 5^k rows are pairwise vertex-disjoint and each has length 7^k. Hölder's inequality on each admissible crossing gives a p-energy contribution at least (7^k)^(1-p), and summing over the disjoint rows yields M_k(p)≥5^k 7^{k(1-p)}. Hence for p<1+log(5)/log(7) the modulus cannot tend to zero, giving Q_LR≥1+log(5)/log(7)=1.827087…. The stated Hausdorff upper bound log(46)/log(7)=1.967532… is standard for the 46-map open-set-condition carpet. The transfer from the combinatorial modulus critical exponent to Ahlfors-regular conformal dimension uses the cited Carrasco-Piaggio/Keith–Laakso framework; for the standard cell approximations of this compact self-similar carpet, no contradictory hypothesis was found.

originality.rationale: The general modulus-to-conformal-dimension machinery is prior work, but the 5-row digit structure and resulting numerical lower edge are specific to this asymmetric 7-adic L-block carpet. Searches of the nearby symmetric-carpet, product-carpet, and general conformal-dimension literature did not locate this exact object or bound, and the numeric edge is not a formal parameter substitution from those results because it depends on the actual retained-row combinatorics.

scientific_value.rationale: The theorem supplies a rigorous, reproducible lower bound for a named asymmetric carpet together with a concrete two-sided localization when combined with its Hausdorff dimension. It does not settle attainment, but it gives a reusable quantitative invariant for subsequent modulus or quasisymmetric-uniformization work. The record clearly separates the proved lower edge from blocked stronger goals.
